title: Island Hopping in Kornati, Croatia: 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Plan island hopping in Kornati National Park: tour prices from €55, park ticket costs, best islands, taverna stops, sailing tips and FAQs for 2027.
content:
## What Is Island Hopping in Kornati?

Kornati National Park covers 89 islands, islets and reefs, which makes it the densest archipelago in the Mediterranean. Almost all of it is uninhabited and treeless, with dry-stone walls, bare limestone and sheer cliffs on the outer side. The locals call these cliffs "crowns". No scheduled ferry or bridge connects the islands, so every visit is by organised boat tour, charter, private boat or kayak.

The park has no gates and no fixed opening hours. It is open all year, but boat services and taverna kitchens run mainly from May to September.

## How to Get to the Kornati Islands

### From Murter

Murter is the closest base. Most excursion boats leave the main port at 09:00 and return between 17:30 and 18:00. The park entrance at Opat is roughly 20 km away, which leaves more time inside the archipelago than departures from Zadar do. The traditional wooden boat Torcida and the boat Re di Mare both run this route.

Typical itinerary: a cruise past the outer cliffs, a swim stop, lunch on board or at Vrulje, and a stop on Levrnaka with a short walk to a viewpoint. The price is €60–65 per adult and €35 for children aged 5–12. Children under 5 go free.

### From Zadar

Zadar tours take about 9 hours and often combine Kornati with Telašćica Nature Park on Dugi Otok. Prices run from about €55 to €70 per adult, usually with breakfast, lunch, drinks and both park tickets. Faster speedboat tours reach the park in about 40 minutes but cost more, around €155.

### From Šibenik, Vodice and Biograd

Biograd na Moru tours start around €60. Vodice tours run closer to €79. Private small-group boats from Šibenik cost considerably more, from about €1,000 per group.

## Kornati National Park Ticket Prices

Park admission is charged per boat per day, not per person. Organised tours include the ticket in the price, so passengers need nothing extra.

- Private boat under 7 m: about €25 low season and €45 high season when bought in advance.
- The same ticket bought from a ranger on the water: about €45 or €90. This is roughly double.
- Kayaks and other non-motorised craft: a reduced fee of about €7 per person per day.
- Larger yachts pay by length, with fees rising steeply above 18 m.

Buy tickets in advance through the park's online shop (np-kornati.hr) or at the park office in Murter. Each day inside the park needs its own ticket.

## Best Islands to Visit

### Levrnaka

Levrnaka has the best swimming in the archipelago. Lojena bay has a sand and pebble beach, which is rare here. A marked path climbs to a viewpoint over the neighbouring islets. Most tour boats stop here, so midday is busy.

### Kornat

Kornat is the largest island, about 25 km long, and gives the park its name. Vrulje bay holds a small fishing settlement with a konoba where tours often serve lunch. Tarac bay has the ruins of a Byzantine fortress from the 6th–7th century. Lavsa, Kravljačica and Vrulje are among the named bays where anchoring and overnight stays are allowed.

### Piškera and Žut

Piškera and Žut each have an ACI marina, and both serve as bases for sailors. Žut sits on the northern edge and works well as a first night stop. Piškera suits a second night deeper in the park.

### Telašćica, Dugi Otok

Telašćica is a separate Nature Park next to Kornati, not part of it. Its draws are the Mir salt lake, which is warmer than the sea, and cliffs that fall about 160 m to the water. Zadar tours nearly always include it.

## Day Tour or Own Boat?

| Option | Cost | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Group day tour | €55–70 per adult | First-time visitors, no sailing licence |
| Private small boat | €25–45 ticket plus rental | Flexible swim stops |
| Skippered charter | Roughly €180–250 per day on top of boat hire | Multi-day trips without sailing skills |
| Sea kayak | €7 per person per day park fee | Fit paddlers staying several days |

A 5-day sailing loop from Zadar covers about 80 nautical miles, with legs of 10 to 25 NM. It suits intermediate sailors.

## Best Time to Go

The best months are May, June and September. Sea temperature is 20–27°C from June to September. July and August bring the most boats, and tour stops such as Lojena bay fill up by late morning. The bora wind can make passages rough, especially outside summer, so check the forecast before leaving Murter or Žut.

## Local Tips

- Buy your park ticket before you enter. Paying a ranger on the water costs about twice as much.
- Choose a Murter departure over a Zadar one if you want time in the park. Zadar tours spend a large share of the day in transit and in Telašćica.
- Ask whether lunch and drinks are included. Prices vary between €55 and €70 mainly because of these extras.
- Some strict-protection zones in the park ban swimming. Surface snorkelling elsewhere needs no permit.
- Bring shoes for rocky landings, a hat and plenty of water. The islands have almost no shade, and signal can be patchy.
- Skip the €155 speedboat tour unless time is tight. The standard boat tour from Murter at about €65 shows the same cliffs and includes lunch, so the extra money buys speed and little else.

## Where to Eat and Stay

The islands have no hotels. Accommodation means a marina berth at Piškera or Žut, an anchorage in a named bay, or a bed in Murter or Zadar. A few family-run konobas in bays such as Vrulje, Lavsa and Statival serve grilled fish, lamb and local cheese, mostly in season. Book ahead if arriving by your own boat in July or August.

## Frequently Asked Questions

See the FAQ section below for quick answers on cost, transport and timing.

faq.question: How much does a Kornati island-hopping tour cost?
faq.answer: A full-day tour costs about €55–70 per adult from Zadar and €60–65 from Murter. Children aged 5–12 usually pay about €35. The park ticket and lunch are normally included.

faq.question: Can you reach the Kornati islands by ferry?
faq.answer: No. No public ferry or bridge serves the park. Visitors go by excursion boat, charter, private boat or kayak.

faq.question: Which town is best for a Kornati day trip?
faq.answer: Murter is the closest, about 20 km from the park entrance at Opat, so the boat spends less time in transit. Zadar offers more tour choices and often adds Telašćica. Šibenik, Vodice and Biograd also have departures.

faq.question: Do you need a ticket for Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: Yes, every visitor needs a valid ticket for each day in the park. Tours include it. Private boats under 7 m pay about €25–45 in advance and roughly double from a ranger on the water.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Kornati?
faq.answer: May, June and September offer calmer crowds and warm water. The sea reaches 20–27°C from June to September. July and August are busiest.

faq.question: Can you stay overnight in Kornati?
faq.answer: Yes, but only on boats in permitted bays such as Lavsa, Vrulje and Kravljačica, or in the ACI marinas at Piškera and Žut. There are no hotels on the islands.

faq.question: Is Telašćica part of Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: No. Telašćica is a separate Nature Park on Dugi Otok with its own entry fee. Many Zadar tours visit both in one day.

quickAnswer: Island hopping in Kornati means visiting a few of the park's 89 islands by boat, because no ferries or bridges serve them. The easiest option is a full-day tour from Murter, Zadar or Šibenik, costing about €55–70 with the park ticket and lunch. Sailing your own boat gives more freedom.
